title: test_seal_is_never_silently_dropped declares PROOF_TIMEOUT_S = 300, so a reseal under sweep load is not read as a timeout red
intention: test_seal_is_never_silently_dropped.py declares a top-level PROOF_TIMEOUT_S = 300, and the tester's run_proof runs it at that budget.
why: Measured 2026-11-19: 2026-11-19, the proof is slow only under load: Windows idle 53 s wall (12 of 12 green, bin/cairn test); Linux idle 23.4 s and 24.2 s (akienasus_cc_0, origin/main 3c6c6c3a1, unsealed, 12 of 12 PASS, no hang); under cc_0's 39-validation reseal sweep on the Dell (22:44-23:05) it exceeded the default 120 s and went red (seal-red-...-test-seal-is-never-silently-dropped). Its own waits are bounded (subprocess timeout=240, bus ask timeout=180), no sleep loop. Law 7: a timeout under load is a measurement of load, not a red of the proof.
traces_to: Law 3 (nothing is known until measured: the budget is measured wall plus margin); Law 4 (the budget is the proof's own byte, physics not a caller's flag).
how: A hypothesis, measured by the proof: add `PROOF_TIMEOUT_S = 300` at the top level of cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_seal_is_never_silently_dropped.py. Budget = measured wall plus margin: the slowest idle wall is 53 s (Windows), so 300 s is 5.7x it and 12.5x the Linux idle; it is 2.5x the 120 s that sweep load already exceeded, so it covers the sweep at up to ~2.5x slowdown beyond the point it timed out. It stays under the proof's own bounded waits summed (240 s + 180 s), so a real hang still reds inside the proof rather than at the budget. If the sweep measures above 300 s the number is re-measured, not guessed up.

clauses.claim: the proof source declares PROOF_TIMEOUT_S as a top-level positive integer, 300, read through the tester's declared_timeout
run_proof on that proof with the reseal door's caller budget of 120 runs at 300: the budget the run records is 300, not 120

decisions.text: D1: test_seal_is_never_silently_dropped.py declares a top-level PROOF_TIMEOUT_S = 300, and the tester's run_proof runs it at that budget.
D2: the red-first proof reads declared_timeout and runs run_proof at a 120 s caller budget, one tooth per clause.

Its own waits are bounded (subprocess timeout=240, bus ask timeout=180), no sleep loop.
